title: Cyber Bureau busts SMC app Ponzi scheme; Chinese national among 11 held
detail: Nepal Police Cyber Bureau arrested 11 people incl. a Chinese national over the 'SMC' movie-trailer app promising 1.2% daily returns; police said over 70,000 users lost about Rs120.8 million. Arrests in Kathmandu, Tarakeshwar, Birgunj and Butwal.
attribution: Nepal Police Cyber Bureau

title: Bus plunges off Prithvi Highway toward Trishuli; 19 dead
detail: A passenger bus left the Prithvi Highway and fell down a slope near the Trishuli River in Dhading, killing at least 19 including a British national and injuring 25.
attribution: Authorities via Al Jazeera

title: Nepal–India border sealed 72 hours for general election
detail: Cross-border movement of people and goods except essentials was halted from Monday midnight for 72 hours ahead of the 5 March House of Representatives election under the Integrated Security Plan, enforced by the Armed Police Force.
attribution: APF DIG Bishnu Prasad Bhatta

title: Three Nepalis rescued from Myawaddy scam centres flown home
detail: The Embassy of Nepal in Bangkok, with Myanmar and Thai authorities, repatriated three Nepalis forced to work in online scam operations in Myawaddy, Myanmar.
attribution: Embassy of Nepal in Bangkok

title: 21 Nepalis from Bavet casino-scam complex repatriated
detail: 21 of 30 Nepalis detained in a 28 January Cambodian police raid on a Bavet casino complex (over 2,000 foreigners held) were repatriated, coordinated by the Nepali embassy in Bangkok and NRNA Cambodia.
attribution: Embassy of Nepal in Bangkok

title: Air Dynasty helicopter crash-lands in Khotang
detail: An Air Dynasty helicopter (9N-AFQ) crash-landed at Belabesi, Khotang; one passenger injured, pilot and four others safe. The operator cited strong wind and dust; investigation pending.
attribution: Operator manager via The Kathmandu Post

title: CIAA charges ex-Speaker Mahara in 9 kg vape-gold smuggling case
detail: CIAA filed charges at the Special Court against former Speaker Krishna Bahadur Mahara over about 9 kg of gold hidden in 730 e-cigarettes at TIA in 2022, seeking recovery of Rs77.86 million; CIB also pursues organised-crime charges.
attribution: Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority

title: Kathmandu ranks among world's 10 most polluted cities
detail: IQAir reported Kathmandu's AQI above 190 ('unhealthy'), citing wildfires and agricultural burning, vehicle and brick-kiln emissions and valley topography.
attribution: IQAir

title: 612 Nepalis rescued from SE Asian scam hubs; 14 detained in Cambodia
detail: MoFA said 612 Nepalis had been rescued and repatriated (Cambodia 487, Myanmar 111, Laos 8, Thailand 6); 9 more Nepalis were arrested in Cambodia on fraud, hostage-taking and torture allegations, bringing those detained there to 14.
attribution: MoFA spokesperson Lok Bahadur Paudel Chhetri

title: Nepal sends notes to India and China over Lipulekh route
detail: MoFA sent diplomatic notes to India and China objecting to reopening the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage/trade route via Lipulekh, restating that Limpiyadhura, Lipulekh and Kalapani belong to Nepal under the 1816 Sugauli Treaty.
attribution: MoFA spokesperson Lok Bahadur Poudel Chhetri

title: APG warns Nepal of blacklist risk over slow AML reforms
detail: An APG delegation led by Deputy Executive Secretary David Shannon found meaningful progress on only 9 of 15 FATF action items and warned failure could lead to blacklisting; it also questioned May 2026 amendments expanding DMLI powers. Exit deadline February 2027.
attribution: APG delegation via The Kathmandu Post

title: 71 more rescued; scam-centre repatriations total 687
detail: MoFA reported 71 more Nepalis rescued, taking the total to 687 (Cambodia 562); the Bangkok embassy secured fine waivers for 102 from Cambodia with 172 pending, while 29 Nepalis remained detained in Cambodia on organised-crime and trafficking charges.
attribution: MoFA spokesperson Lok Bahadur Poudel Chhetri

title: DHM forecasts below-normal, hotter monsoon
detail: DHM's National Outlook for Monsoon Season 2026 forecast below-normal rainfall and above-normal temperatures across most of Nepal due to El Niño, while warning intense localised rain can still cause floods and landslides.
attribution: DHM Director General Archana Shrestha

title: 23 arrested with drugs across seven districts
detail: Nepal Police arrested 23 people with brown sugar, cannabis and prescription tablets, 11 of them in Kathmandu and 6 in Jhapa.
attribution: Nepal Police

title: Nepal stays on FATF grey list after June review
detail: FATF kept Nepal under increased monitoring; outstanding items include risk-based supervision of banks, cooperatives, casinos and real estate, more ML prosecutions, and sanctioning illegal money transfer (hundi) services.
attribution: FATF review report via The Kathmandu Post

title: 775 kg of marijuana found under potato sacks in Koshi
detail: Koshi Province Police arrested five and seized 795 kg of marijuana, 775 kg of it in a mini-truck intercepted at Sangurigadhi RM, Dhankuta.
attribution: SSP Yogendra Singh Thapa, Koshi Province Police

title: Monsoon landslides kill infant in Dolakha and woman in Jajarkot
detail: Rain-triggered landslides killed a four-month-old in Kalinchok, Dolakha and a 60-year-old woman in Bheri Municipality, Jajarkot on 12–13 July, per local reports.
attribution: Local officials via The Kathmandu Post

title: Tatopani crossing shut as Araniko/Kodari Highway subsides
detail: The Tatopani–Zhangmu crossing closed after the Kodari Highway subsided about two metres at Iko, Bhotekoshi RM, leaving dozens of cargo containers stuck on the Chinese side.
attribution: Local officials via The Kathmandu Post

title: DHM warns of heavy to very heavy rain in six provinces
detail: DHM warned of heavy to very heavy rainfall over 19–20 July in Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki, Lumbini and Sudurpaschim, citing a Bay of Bengal low and a northward monsoon trough; flood, landslide and urban inundation risk flagged.
attribution: DHM

title: Communal unrest in Sunsari and Siraha leaves three dead; curfew
detail: A Hindu–Muslim dispute over music and flags during a procession escalated; police shot two men in Sunsari and one man died in a Siraha protest. Curfew imposed in Sunsari and neighbouring areas; PM Balendra Shah appealed for calm and promised an investigation.
attribution: Nepal Police and PM Balendra Shah, via Al Jazeera

title: Susta standoff after SSB dismantles flood embankment
detail: Indian SSB personnel dismantled a makeshift earthen flood embankment built by residents in disputed Susta; Indian side said a crowd of 150–200 pelted stones at the patrol, no injuries reported. Nepal's APF intervened and Kathmandu raised the matter with New Delhi.
agency: Armed Police Force; Sashastra Seema Bal
attribution: CDO Dipak Raj Nepal via The Kathmandu Post; SSB account via ETV Bharat

title: NCB Nepalgunj seizes 579 g brown sugar sourced from India
detail: Narcotics Control Bureau's Nepalgunj office arrested two men with nearly 579 g of brown sugar, Rs180,000 and INR 214,000; police said it was sourced from Bahraich, India for Karnali and Lumbini.
attribution: Narcotics Control Bureau

title: Glacier collapse triggers catastrophic Rasuwa–Trishuli flood
detail: A glacial collapse sent ice, rock and debris into the Lhende Khola, unleashing a flood down the Bhotekoshi/Trishuli valley that destroyed the Gyirong/Rasuwagadhi border area; at least 469 deaths in Nepal were reported by 28 August, with over 1,500 missing across Nepal and Tibet.
attribution: Al Jazeera/Reuters citing Nepali authorities

title: USGS characterises Langtang debris avalanche
detail: USGS said the event was likely triggered by rapid slope failure involving a glacier in Langtang National Park, releasing energy equal to an M5.2 quake with a secondary M4.2 signal three hours later, and travelling about 100 km downstream past the Rasuwagadhi border post.
attribution: USGS

title: Flood destroys Rasuwagadhi–Kerung crossing, Nepal's main China trade gateway
detail: The flood destroyed the Rasuwagadhi checkpoint, Sino-Nepal Friendship Bridge and dry port; the route had carried 60–70 cargo vehicles a day, and customs officials said about 176 containers were stranded in Kerung, with trade to be rerouted via Tatopani or Korala.
attribution: Customs officials via The Kathmandu Post

title: China warns of barrier lake upstream of Bhotekoshi
detail: China's Ministry of Water Resources warned via CCTV that a ~2 million cubic metre barrier lake near the Chhochen Khola–Purepu Tsangpo confluence was overflowing and at high risk of breaching, with 3 million m3 more inflow expected; Nepali authorities restricted highway movement and moved residents downstream.
attribution: China Ministry of Water Resources via CCTV, reported by The Kathmandu Post

title: Flood wrecks hydropower, roads; reconstruction put at $4–5bn
detail: Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle gave a preliminary reconstruction estimate of US$4–5 billion (about Rs762 billion); roughly 15,000 houses destroyed, multiple hydropower plants damaged and road links to Dhunche and Syafrubesi severed; NDRRMA rapid assessment under way, PDNA expected to take two months.
attribution: Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and NPC Vice-chair Gunakhar Bhatta, via The Kathmandu Post

title: Bhotekoshi–Trishuli flood toll reaches 1,355
detail: NDRRMA put the toll at 1,355 dead, 6,672 treated for injuries and 4,996 unaccounted for across eight districts (Chitwan 363 deaths, Nawalparasi East 222, Nawalparasi West 221), with 13,396 rescued; preliminary losses Rs387.5 billion (about US$2.56 billion).
attribution: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, via The Kathmandu Post

title: Gen Z uprising anniversary gathering in Baneshwar
detail: Gen Z activists and victims' families gathered at the former Parliament building to mark one year since the September 2025 uprising; PM Shah was absent and Home Minister Sudan Gurung attended. Karki Commission recommendations remain largely unprosecuted.
attribution: The Kathmandu Post

title: Heavy to very heavy rain forecast for 24–28 September
detail: DHM's Meteorological Forecasting Division warned of heavy to very heavy rain over 24–28 September, heaviest in western and central Nepal; some models showed 400–741 mm. The 2026 monsoon entered Nepal on 19 June, six days late.
attribution: DHM Meteorological Forecasting Division; model figures per meteorologist Binod Pokharel
